main_body: Stone brick wall/paving pattern filling the whole 68x48 tile: beveled taupe bricks in staggered courses with dark mortar lines
top_band: none: a flat tiling surface; each brick has only a 1px light top and left bevel, with no separate top surface above a front face
evidence: The kind is terrain (a seamless tile, not a standing object), so the top-band and front-face contract does not apply. The column reads brick face, mortar, brick face, with no standing volume to judge. Each brick has a light bevel on the top and left and a darker mortar shadow below and right, which is the normal construction for a terrain tile.

style.evidence: The mortar lines are a dark purple-brown tinted to match the stone, not near-black, which is good. The bricks use only about 4 tones (pale tan bevel, mid taupe face, dark mortar, deepest shadow), plus a few sparse light and dark speckle dots. Each brick face is a large near-flat mid-tone area of roughly 12x7 px with only 2-3 dots. The cobble reference has per-stone shading and grain and carries more colours per 16x16 tile. This tile reads cleaner and flatter, with a uniform repeating bevel, so it looks thinner next to the reference.
